consumer credit-bureau score only (drops business 'Commercial Bureau' and 'None' score types; each lender labels the consumer score its own way)

originated at most 12 months before the deal's first pool filing — older loans still in a pool are survivors of years of payoffs and defaults
loan amount and vehicle value above $1,000
origination month has a Treasury benchmark
vehicle model year plausible (1990 to origination year + 1)

reasons: Your credit score of 660 raises the typical rate by about 3.2 points compared with a typical credit score of 719.
A car 7 years old raises the typical rate by about 0.7 points compared with a typical 3-year-old car.
Borrowing $18,500 raises the typical rate by about 0.4 points compared with borrowing a typical $25,382.
weak_spots: The data has no race, sex or age and no dealer details, so the tool can show how far a price is from similar loans, but not why.
Credit unions and banks that don't sell their loans into public bonds appear only as national averages, not loan by loan.
jordan.data_note: Compared with 554,021 loans from 28 SEC-filed bond deals (Ally, American Honda Finance, Capital One, CarMax Auto Finance, Ford Credit, GM Financial, Hyundai Capital America, Nissan Motor Acceptance, Santander Consumer, Toyota Financial Services), originated 2023-01 to 2026-01. Prices are compared after removing the 5-year Treasury rate; your offer uses the 2026-10 average of 4.93%.
